sonic_perspective.listener: fixed in the man's room, at his head, for the whole pass; never moves with the camera
sonic_perspective.room_tone: his room: one continuous, unlooped foraged room tone, constant gain, no fades inside the pass (1 s RMS -42.5..-41.4 dBFS)
sonic_perspective.bell: in another room/hall: the crank magneto bell heard THROUGH THE WALL (HP 150 Hz, LP 2.5 kHz 36 dB/oct, handmade room IR RT60 0.55 s wet 0.45), peak -8 dB rel the near footfalls
sonic_perspective.near_footfalls: S5/S7: closer and drier than the bell (no reverb, full band), placed unstretched at the beats times; they are the reference level (0 dB rel, peak -6 dBFS)
sonic_perspective.stairwell_footfalls: S6: two footfalls further up the well, -12 dB rel (post-chain peak), LP 2.5 kHz, handmade stairwell IR RT60 1.4 s wet 0.7, gated to silence by 27.0
sonic_perspective.withheld: E1 (the wake, 2.0-2.8) has no sound cue: only room tone 1.5-3.3 (non-room stems peak 0.0). SIL-H 11.5-19.0 is room tone only.
sonic_perspective.level_rule: all relative levels are post-chain sample peaks against the near-footfall reference REF = -6 dBFS

evidence.title: WWS Minetelephone
evidence.author: Work With Sounds / Konrad Gutkowski (Work With Sounds cooperation with Wikimedia Sverige)
evidence.what_it_shows: A Funke & Huster crank (magneto) mine telephone: handset clunk at 0.75 s, then the bell trill 2.85-20.15 s and its natural ring-off to ~20.75 s (21.1 s, 44.1 kHz stereo Vorbis). Strong partials near 2.2, 4.1-4.4 and 5.3 kHz. No voice, no music (spectrogram work/spec_wws_mine_telephone.ogg.png). A magneto bell matching the S2 crank wall phone, as the plan preferred.
evidence.verified_date_or_place: Recorded 2014-03-06 (Commons DateTimeOriginal), LWL-Industrial Museum Zollern Colliery, Dortmund, Germany (Commons description)
evidence.reuse_note: same file the r1 U2 unit downloaded; SHA-1 re-checked against Commons today; licence re-read from extmetadata today

evidence.title: Wooden stairs (Gravity Sound)
evidence.author: Gravity Sound
evidence.what_it_shows: One walker on a wooden staircase, ~0.75 s step period, board creaks, 26 s. No voice, no music (spectrogram work/spec_steps_wooden_gravity.wav.mp3.png; harmonicity check 0 frames > 0.6 on the near stem).

evidence.used_as: near footfalls (src onsets 7.399, 12.185, 14.585, 16.905, 19.12; 0.46 s windows, unstretched) at 20.8/21.35/21.9/22.45/23.0 and identically at 28.8/29.35/29.9/30.45/31.0; stairwell footfalls (src onsets ~3.355 and ~4.375) at 25.2 and 25.95

moving_image_archive_listening.method: every clip with audio among the hits that could plausibly carry room hush, a bell or footsteps was decoded with ffmpeg and examined: 40 ms harmonicity (speech/music pitch) and level frames, longest unvoiced stretch, spectrogram (mia/spec_*.png) and a frame strip (mia/frames_*.jpg)

candidates.title: Door to Heaven, The (1941)
candidates.why: narration throughout (16% voiced frames); the longest unvoiced stretch (16.9-21.2 s) carries a sustained ~1 kHz tonal line with harmonics (music or print tone), not room tone; picture is a dim curtained room

candidates.title: Alcohol and the Human Body (1949)
candidates.why: narration; the speech-free gaps (8.4-11.7 s, 16.5-20.5 s) are <=4 s of optical-track hum (steady 100-500 Hz lines), i.e. print noise, not a room; 35 s continuous would need ~9 seams

candidates.title: Learning to Set Type (1959)
candidates.why: narration bursts with a steady print hum between; 11.6 s gap is hum, not room; 1959 rights not established

candidates.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4)
candidates.why: silent amateur film: the track is a steady -53 dBFS transfer rumble (no room acoustics); it is telecine noise, not a recording of a place

candidates.title: We Learn About the Telephone I (1965)
candidates.why: dense music/effects bed, no isolable bell; 1965 rights not established

candidates.title: Communications and Our Town (1947)
candidates.why: church bells under narration (32% voiced); bells are not a telephone bell

candidates.title: Third Avenue El (n.d.)
candidates.why: 3.2 s; tonal lines (music/train), no footsteps isolable; year unknown and rights unclear

handmade stairwell IR RT60 1.4 s, wet 0.7; LP 2.5 kHz; gated to zero by 27.0

SIL-H_verdict: pass: non-zero floor (RMS -41.96 dBFS), max 50 ms transient 2.64 dB and max 10 ms transient 5.33 dB above the median floor (4.81 dB above RMS), all <= 6 dB; no non-room stem has a non-zero sample in 11.5-19.0

voicing.ST-BELL_note: the bell is a pitched periodic source, so harmonicity is high by nature; speech is excluded by the source (a mechanical bell, no persons in the recording) and by the spectrogram

audibility_measured.bell_body_rms_dbfs: R1 -30.8, R2 -28.4, R3 -29.8 vs room -42.0; in-band (2.0-2.5 kHz) 26-33 dB over room
audibility_measured.bell_after_E3: the R3 bell's own ring-off and reverb run to 10.88 (E3 t_off 10.0, head returns 10.4); nothing after 11.0

speech_music_statement: No speech and no music is audible in any stem (measured: room/near/stairwell stems have no 40 ms frame with pitch harmonicity > 0.6 except 40 ms in the stairwell reverb tail, max 0.707; the bell is a pitched mechanical source by nature; spectrograms inspected). Perceptual listening by a human has NOT occurred; this is measured and spectrogram-inspected only.
deviations_from_plan: Levels are defined as post-chain sample peaks against the near footfalls (REF -6 dBFS). With the r1 room level (-40 dBFS RMS) and a -12 dB stairwell cue the S6 footfalls measured 2-8 dB BELOW the room's own 10 ms peaks (inaudible). r2 lowers the room tone to -42 dBFS RMS and raises REF from -12 to -6 dBFS; the plan's relative -8 dB (bell) and -12 dB (stairwell) are kept exactly.
Ring 3 keeps the bell's real ring-off (to 10.6 + reverb to 10.88) after the cranking stops at 10.0, rather than a cut.
Stairwell footfalls at 25.2 and 25.95 (S6 is not bound to picture events in beats-r2), gated to zero by 27.0.
